title: BL1: boosted-leaf linear-merge collimation with Q = O(2^(sqrt n)), T = O(n^5 2^((3/2) sqrt n)), S_C = O(n^3 2^((3/2) sqrt n)) and O(n) qubits

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single BL1 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch for n < 64; otherwise leaf tables of kappa+1+v leaf qubits with w = ceil(sqrt n), kappa = ceil(log2 w) + 1 and v = ceil(w/2) + 6 kappa, table lengths growing by one bit per level below the root, with no width cap, on a linear-merge collimation tree of depth at most w, and at most w - 4 kappa for n >= 2^24, free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its total charged sequential work is T(N,s) = O(n^5 2^((3/2) sqrt n)), with the uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = n^5 2^((3/2) sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. The inner coefficient is exact, not an unknown big-O constant. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single BL1 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch for n < 64; otherwise leaf tables of kappa+1+v leaf qubits with w = ceil(sqrt n), kappa = ceil(log2 w) + 1 and v = ceil(w/2) + 6 kappa, table lengths growing by one bit per level below the root, with no width cap, on a linear-merge collimation tree of depth at most w, and at most w - 4 kappa for n >= 2^24, free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(n^3 2^((3/2) sqrt n)) bits, with envelope B_C(n) = n^3 2^((3/2) sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. The inner coefficient is exact, not an unknown big-O constant. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single BL1 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch for n < 64; otherwise leaf tables of kappa+1+v leaf qubits with w = ceil(sqrt n), kappa = ceil(log2 w) + 1 and v = ceil(w/2) + 6 kappa, table lengths growing by one bit per level below the root, with no width cap, on a linear-merge collimation tree of depth at most w, and at most w - 4 kappa for n >= 2^24, free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with envelope B_Q(n) = n, whose exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single BL1 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch for n < 64; otherwise leaf tables of kappa+1+v leaf qubits with w = ceil(sqrt n), kappa = ceil(log2 w) + 1 and v = ceil(w/2) + 6 kappa, table lengths growing by one bit per level below the root, with no width cap, on a linear-merge collimation tree of depth at most w, and at most w - 4 kappa for n >= 2^24, free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh source copies acquired, counting every discarded, rejected and failed-attempt copy, is at most N(n+10) on the finite branch n < 64 and at most the precomputed cap Qcap = 1024 Q*, Q* = 6 * 2^mmax (kappa+1+v) ((J+1)K + 2 a2) + 2 a2 (proof.md Section 11; a2 is the 2-adic valuation of N, J and K are from proof.md Section 9, mmax from Section 7), on the main branch n >= 64, where mmax <= w - 4 kappa for n >= 2^24 gives Qcap = O(2^(sqrt n)) (proof.md Sections 7 and 13). Hence Q(N,s) = O(2^(sqrt n)), with envelope B_samples(n) = 2^(sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. The inner coefficient is exact, not an unknown big-O constant. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For the same BL1 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
